title: app-riset-pdp: Client-Side Face Detection Benchmarking Instrument (OpenCV.js vs face-api.js)
description:
A self-contained, client-side face detection benchmarking instrument (single HTML/JavaScript page, no build step, no server-side biometric processing) that compares two in-browser face detection pipelines: OpenCV.js (Haar Cascade + LBP histogram + cosine similarity, threshold >= 0.85) and face-api.js (TinyFaceDetector + 68-point landmarks + 128-D descriptor + euclidean distance, threshold <= 0.60), under a controlled 36-scenario factorial design (3 lighting levels x 4 pose angles x 3 device tiers).

Features dual-engine identity enrollment; manual and automated (36-scenario) trial capture with optional manual-confirmation gating between scenarios; live per-engine latency/FPS-equivalent/memory metrics; aggregate and per-scenario precision/recall/F1-score summaries; CSV/JSON export of raw and summarized logs; and a client-vs-server comparison module that calls a real companion API (api-riset-pdp, Cloudflare Workers) or simulates the server-side pathway from network parameters (RTT, upload/download bandwidth, server processing time).

All biometric processing runs entirely in the browser, in line with a privacy-by-design architecture. Developed as the data-collection instrument for the study 'Inovasi Media ICT Deteksi Wajah untuk Presensi Digital Mahasiswa: Analisis Akurasi dan Performa' (Sismadi, Manan, & Hartini, 2026, ACADEMIA: Jurnal Inovasi Riset Akademik, 6(4), 3400-3408), conducted under the Penelitian Dosen Pemula (PDP) grant at Universitas IPWIJA, Jakarta, with 50 student participants and 180 observations per library in a closed-set verification scenario.
